answer: A tiered stake-and-service bond works well: each agent locks a deposit that grows as it climbs each terrace of trust, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts on the lowest terrace with tiny transaction limits, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of separate bonds while the payoff stays small. Honest agents instead accumulate nectar, reputation credit earned only from verified completed work, which leaves a plume of auditable evidence behind every deal. Forging that history costs real work and real money, so sybils stop paying.
